General Funding Opportunities

We support students through several different funding schemes, including University and external scholarships. Many of these are open to both UK and international-fee students.

Applicants to our PhD programmes will be automatically considered for funding through the University scholarships, and Research Council studentships. Some other schemes require additional actions as described below.

In order to be considered for a funded position, candidates must have submitted an application before the programme-specific deadline as advertised on DegreeFinder  (generally early January for Astronomy, and mid-January for Physics).
Note that the Bell-Burnell Graduate Scholarship Fund has an earlier deadline of 27 November 2026. 

To ensure your application is directed to the relevant admissions coordinators, please ensure you indicate in your application which research area(s) you are applying for:

  • Astronomy (Astro)
  • Hard Condensed Matter (including computational materials physics, extreme conditions, quantum ordering) (Hard CM)
  • Soft Matter (including statistical physics, biophysics, astrobiology) (Soft CM)
  • Physics Education Research (PER)
  • Nuclear Physics (NP)
  • Particle Physics Experiment (PPE)
  • Particle Physics Theory (PPT)

University-funded studentships

The School of Physics & Astronomy has a number of fully funded studentships, available in all subject areas. All applicants who have submitted an application by the deadline listed on the relevant Degree Finder page will be considered for these awards. These scholarships cover the University tuition fee as well as a stipend equal to the UKRI minimum rate, for the relevant academic year of study. Students are also supported by a training grant of £1.2k/year to cover research costs, books, computing, and travel. Subject to satisfactory progress, these Scholarships are offered for 3.5 years. 

Applicants are automatically considered for any other University-funded scholarships which they are eligible for. This includes the Edinburgh Doctoral College Scholarships.

We welcome applications from both home and international fee-rate students for these awards.

Career Development Scholarship

The School of Physics and Astronomy Career Development Scholarship (CDS) provides full PhD funding for students from a Black heritage, including mixed Black background.  We welcome applications from prospective students, both UK and International. 

In addition to the standard application form, students must complete a separate form to declare interest and confirm eligibility. Full information is available on the dedicated CDS web page.

Bell-Burnell Graduate Scholarship Fund

We support candidates for the Institute of Physics Bell-Burnell Graduate Scholarship Fund(link is external). To be considered, candidates must have (1) applied through our main PhD application portal by 27 November 2026 and (2) sent a one-page CV and a 1-2 page personal statement to the Graduate School office (Gradschool.Physics [at] ed.ac.uk) and the relevant PhD coordinator for their research area: 

  • Astronomy: Trent Dupuy (tdupuy [at] roe.ac.uk)
  • Condensed Matter, including soft matter, statistical physics, biophysics, astrobiology, hard condensed matter, physics education research: Simon Titmuss (simon.titmuss [at] ed.ac.uk) and Dominique Laniel (Dominique.Laniel [at] ed.ac.uk)
  • Nuclear Physics: Pascal Reiter (mreiter [at] ed.ac.uk)
  • Particle Physics Experiment: Cheryl Patrick (cpatrick [at] exseed.ed.ac.uk)
  • Particle Physics Theory: Tej Kanwar (gkanwar [at] ed.ac.uk)

Following the BBGSF scheme, the personal statement should describe (a) your reasons for wanting to study for a Doctorate; (b) how you meet the BBGSF eligibility criteria clearly stating which under-represented group you identify as; (c) how you propose to gain benefit from a grant, if awarded (d) how you would be an ambassador for the scheme.

Shortlisted candidates will be invited to interview during the week of December 14.

Up to two selected candidates will be nominated to apply for the BBGSF scheme, with an external deadline of January 18. Nominees will then be considered for available fully-funded scholarships managed by the University, with the outcome announced by March. 

Research Council Studentships

The School also offers fully funded studentships awarded by United Kingdom Research and Innovation (UKRI) Doctoral Landscape Awards (DLAs). All applicants who have submitted an application by the deadline listed on the relevant Degree Finder page will be considered for these awards - there is no requirement for a separate application.

We have a number of fully-funded studentships from UKRI Doctoral Landscape Awards (DLAs), covering STFC and EPSRC councils: 

  • EPSRC
  • STFC

We also support students applying for UKRI doctoral networks, both DLAs and Doctoral Focal Awards (DFA / CDT). These include, but are not limited to:

PLANET (Physics-Led Applications for Nuclear Engineering & Technology)

The PLANET programme - a Doctoral Focal Award by UK Research and Innovation (UKRI) and match-funded by industry - will equip students and researchers to work in fields vital to national security, clean energy and healthcare. 

PLANET is a UK partnership consisting of word class nuclear physics research groups (Universities of Edinburgh, Surrey and York), and premier nuclear engineering groups (Universities of Cambridge and Lancaster).

The projects are co-created with industry and include professional skills training and an industrial placement. Projects will train researchers in areas such as nuclear science, neutron and radiation transport, simulation and instrumentation development.

Application deadline: TBC for September 2027 entry.

Further information and application details are located on the PLANET site:

PLANET

The PLANET team are hosting a webinar for potential applicants, on Tuesday 24th November.

More information and the link to register can be found at the following link: PLANET Application Webinar.

Mathematical Modelling, Analysis and Computation

The Mathematical Modelling, Analysis and Computation (MAC-MIGS) Centre for Doctoral Training is offering around 15 studentships PhD students an intensive 4-year training and research programme that equips them with the skills needed to tackle the challenges of data-intensive modelling.

Strong applicants with interests relevant to all areas of mathematical modelling, analysis and computing, as well as students whose first degree is in other fields of science and engineering, are encouraged to apply.

MAC-MIGS is a PhD programme run jointly by the universities of Edinburgh and Heriot-Watt, as part of the Maxwell Institute Graduate School. MAC-MIGS projects are focussed on the formulation, analysis and implementation of state-of-the-art mathematical and computational models and methods.  The Centre aims to train modelling experts who can develop and analyse mathematical models, translate them into efficient computer codes, and communicate the solutions with industry and government. MAC-MIGS will be based in new Bayes Centre on the University of Edinburgh's central campus, the heart of the £1B Edinburgh City Deal.

Visit the MAC-MIGS webpage for application deadlines: Application deadlines

Further information on the MAC-MIGS CDT.

Quantum Informatics CDT

The new Centre for Doctoral Training in Quantum Informatics will provide advanced training in the structure, behaviour and interaction of quantum hardware, software, and applications. The training programme spans computer sciences, mathematics, physics and engineering. The programme offers a fully funded intensive 4-year PhD with integrated study programme that equips students with the skills need to tackle the research challenges of quantum informatics. The programme includes bespoke training by the National Quantum Computing Centre, and the opportunity to work with over 30 industry partners. Graduates will be able to integrate quantum hardware with high-performance computing, design effective quantum software and apply this in a societally meaningful way.
